newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures surge after spot Sept expiry.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures surge after spot Sept expiry.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures surged by their daily limit on Friday as the strong expiry of spot September triggered waves of heavy buying, traders said.
The spot September contract expired late morning at 16,520 yen, up by 950 yen from the previous day's close. A total 122 lots deliveries were made.
Benchmark July 1998 closed up by its 400 yen per tonne daily limit at 15,210 yen.
Heavy buying orders from local investors emerged in the afternoon encouraged by the spot month's sharply higher expiry price, traders said.
"The yen's weaker tone also accelerated bullish sentiment," a brokerage house analyst said.
The spot September corn contract on the CBOT Project A trading system stood at $2.65 per bushel at 0725 GMT, against $2.64-1/4 from Thursday's close.
Spot August CBOT soybean futures were at $7.78 per bushel at 0725 GMT, against $7.72-1/2 at Thursday's close.
